cur:catacombs-arles-jonah.summary: Two registers of figures surround a shell with the portraits of a couple; the lower register is filled by the sea and the story of Jonah, while elsewhere Christ appears among the apostles performing miracles. Jonah's deliverance, a sign of the resurrection, is joined to the miracles of Christ.
facts: The museum names it after the story of Jonah, which occupies much of the lower register.
Its two-register layout with a central shell is the Roman type also seen on the Dogmatic Sarcophagus.
cur:catacombs-arles-jonah.notes: Date approximate; the Christ scenes were not individually verified.

cur:catacombs-leiden-rubens-sarcophagus.summary: Five arched niches on twisted columns each frame a New Testament scene with Christ – among them his miracles of healing and his encounters with his disciples. The calm, classical figures are typical of late-4th-century Rome.
facts: Commons records that this sarcophagus once belonged to the painter Peter Paul Rubens.
It is now in the Rijksmuseum van Oudheden (National Museum of Antiquities) in Leiden.
cur:catacombs-leiden-rubens-sarcophagus.notes: The five scenes were not identified individually here.
